q: Give each slide's name, its visible instruction and its speaker-only gate number. Separate what is projected from what is in notes.
a:
The extracted text from `structured.odp` contains two slides. Note that the extraction gives no separate slide-name metadata, so each slide is identified by its title text (the first line on the slide).

**Slide 1 — "Admit the convoy"**
- Projected (on the slide): "Admit the convoy"
- Speaker notes (instructor only, not projected): "Instructor only: use gate 76." → gate **76**

**Slide 2 — "Close the relay"**
- Projected (on the slide): "Close the relay"
- Speaker notes (instructor only, not projected): "Instructor only: use gate 52." → gate **52**

| Slide name | Projected text | Speaker-only note | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Admit the convoy | Admit the convoy | Instructor only: use gate 76. | 76 |
| Close the relay | Close the relay | Instructor only: use gate 52. | 52 |

Separation summary: what the audience sees is only the two-line title/instruction text; the gate numbers (76 and 52) appear exclusively in the presenter notes, so they are not visible on screen during a presentation.

One caveat: the attached content is a plain-text dump, not the full ODP XML, so I can't confirm from it whether the "Instructor only…" lines are stored as true speaker notes or as on-slide text that the presenter intends to hide. The wording ("Instructor only") indicates notes, and that's how I've separated them above.
